text:
Marathon Petroleum stock rose 0.69% today to close at $424.89, continuing a sharp nine-day rally that's now up nearly 10%. The stock has climbed steadily since mid-September as oil prices have spiked—US crude is now trading at $107 per barrel, up sharply from earlier in the month—while US refineries are operating at 96.8% capacity. For a refiner like Marathon, higher crude prices typically lift margins when the company can process and sell refined products (gasoline and diesel) at profitable spreads, especially when refineries are running hot.

The rally reflects a confluence of supply fears from Middle East tensions: Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure, Iranian threats to the Strait of Hormuz, and Pakistani concerns over energy supplies have all weighed on oil markets over the past week. Though oil fell slightly on Monday as traders noted Saudi crude flows remain "surprisingly strong," the geopolitical premium—the extra cost baked into prices due to conflict risk—remains embedded in these prices, supporting refiner economics as long as refineries can keep running full.
